summary: Assist with optimizer 'drift detector' and stepwise rollback after latency and instruction-quality regression
description:
Issue summary: CartaHealth reports a simultaneous rise in 95th-percentile token latency and a measurable drop in instruction-following quality after we applied a tenant-scoped optimizer profile (aggressive batching + KV-prefetch + quant-profile v2) on 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC. Impact: degradation impacts two critical endpoints used in production EHR summarization workflows — these are latency-sensitive and quality-sensitive (mis-summarizations are patient-risk relevant). Timeline: 2026-03-09 22:30 - optimizer profile applied via console rollout API; 2026-03-09 23:05 - first alert on latency > SLA for tenant; 2026-03-10 - customer opened support case. Customer request: guidance for a controlled, stepwise rollback (safest possible path) and assistance with setting up a short-lived "drift detector" to alert on further quality or latency regression during any changes. They would prefer per-tenant incremental toggles and a low-risk path (no full cluster restarts). They are on a Dedicated plan with reserved pools and cannot tolerate prolonged service interruptions.

Notes: This ticket should be treated as operationally urgent for the tenant (P1) but not a platform-wide incident. Avoid global toggles. Preference for snapshot-based restoration and non-disruptive config flips.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target tenant: carta-tenant-42 on prod us-east-1
2) Apply optimizer profile: aggressive-batch-prefetch-quant-v2 via /tenant-configs API (example payload attached in comment)
3) Send representative production traffic (EHR summarization route, 1.2 RPS average, peak 8 RPS bursty)
4) Observe increase in 95p token-latency and drop in BLEU/ROUGE-like evals from nightly sampling (we provided sample prompts)
5) Reproduce locally by toggling per-tenant kv_prefetch=true and batch_window_ms=25 with quant_profile=q4f16-strict on a staging replica
logs: [2026-03-09T23:07:12Z] optimizer: applied profile aggressive-batch-prefetch-quant-v2 to tenant carta-tenant-42
[2026-03-09T23:09:01Z] kv_cache: miss_rate increased to 0.48 from 0.12 for tenant carta-tenant-42
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: aggressive batching increased tail latency during bursty traffic because batch_window_ms=25ms causes queuing; warmup not sufficient for KV-prefetch pattern.
Hypothesis B: quant-profile q4f16-strict interacts with KV cache prefetch causing cache fragmentation and higher miss rates for long-context EHR prompts.
Telemetry: per-tenant KV miss rate correlation with latency spike observed (pearson r=0.71). Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/tenant-latency/carta-tenant-42
We ran a controlled canary on a staging replica toggling batch_window_ms from 25->10ms and observed 95p drop from 390ms->220ms but throughput dropped ~7% under synthetic burst traffic.
Quant toggles on a small sample saw slight quality improvement but increased token compute by ~11% (expected due to conservative kernels).
No hardware OOMs or CUDA errors in node logs; GPU utilization stable. Scheduler logs show no recent preemptions for the tenant's reserved pool.
mitigation: 1) Immediate customer-safe action (non-disruptive): roll back tenant optimizer profile to previous snapshot: baseline-2026-03-08-2100 using tenant-configs API with dry-run then apply.

2) If rollback is not acceptable to customer, apply stepwise toggles: a) reduce batch_window_ms 25 -> 12 -> 8 in 2-minute steps b) disable kv_prefetch for 10 minutes and monitor c) switch quant_profile q4f16-strict -> q4f16-balanced for 1h canary
3) Create temporary drift detector: a server-side policy that samples 1% of requests for instruction-quality evals and alerts if BLEU/ROUGE-like drop >3% or 95p latency >250ms for 10min window
4) Instrument per-tenant telemetry alerts and start a 30-minute monitoring run after each toggle with SLO guardrails (auto-rollforward if errors increase).
5) If stepwise toggles fix latency but quality remains degraded, plan snapshot restore of model serving config and schedule a quiet maintenance window for deeper rollback.
resolution: Pending customer approval for one of two safe paths. We prepared an automated script that will: 1) perform a dry-run restoration to baseline-2026-03-08-2100; 2) execute an incremental toggle sequence (batch_window_ms then kv_prefetch then quant_profile); and 3) enable the drift-detector for 24 hours. Engineering prepared a per-tenant config snapshot so that rollback is atomic and reversible. Customer requested we first attempt the non-destructive stepwise toggles; support will run them 2026-03-12 01:00 UTC and remain on call. After successful rollback, follow-up actions: add per-tenant canary automation and create runbook SUP-13579-RB for cross-training.
